Title: [3D Tool] Free Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing.

Title: Plot Patterns (Above ver4.2.0)
Content: List of Contents Plot Patterns Recommended Plotter Specifications Objective Plot 2D Patterns to manufacture real garments. Location Main Menu File Plotter Operation Plot Patterns Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. The Plotter window appears as the mode is switched to the Print Layout Mode to arrange Patterns based on the paper size. Select types of segments and information that will be plotted. Option Description Cut on Outline Patterns are cut based on the outlines or seam allowances. Note: Notches are cut when they exist on Patterns. Show Lines Select types of lines that would appear on the prints. Show Add'l Information Select information that would appear on prints. Click Plot. Patterns are plotted according to the setting. Note: Select the plotter or network plotter to be integrated with CLO in the Other setting. To save as a .plt file, please follow below paths: Main Menu File Plotter Save from the dialogue (Usable only in Window) Main Menu File Export Plotter (PLT) Recommended Plotter Specifications Recommended Model: Model: Graphtec CE-6000AP OS: Windows Only Port: RS-232C Language: HP-GL

Title: [3D Tool] 1:N Free Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Line appears in neon color. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. Release the Shift key to complete. Note While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: [3D Tool] 1:N Segment Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. Note While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: [3D Tool] M:N Free Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Free Sewing Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Free Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied.

Title: [3D Tool] M:N Segment Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment.

Title: [Popup] Copy/Paste Tack
Content: List of Contents Copy/Paste Tack Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Objective Copy and paste tack. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack Operation Copy/Paste Tack Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Copy The selected tack is copied. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. Select Paste or Mirror Paste. Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. Any tack outside of the Pattern do not appear in the 3D window. Click the desired location to paste the tack. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the tack to be duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. Selected tack is duplicated to the exact same location on its Symmetric Pattern. Note: Select tacks need to be within the same Pattern in order to be duplicated to their Symmetric Patterns.

Title: [Property] Register Custom Image as Buttonhole
Content: Objective Register a custom image as a buttonhole. Location Main Menu Materials Button Register Buttonhole Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a Buttonhole Style Property Editor Shape Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu Materials Button Register Buttonhole Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a Buttonhole Style Property Editor Shape The Create Buttonhole window appears. Enter its name in the Name field. Click the button next to the Image option. The File Browser appears. Select an image to be used as a buttonhole. Fill in all required fields and click OK. Registered buttonhole is automatically added to Property Editor Shape. Registered buttonhole is saved in CLO-ENTERPRISE Assets_ver.x.x.xx Preferences Buttons_Preset.

Title: [Popup] Button Right-Click Menus
Content: Objective Change status of buttons as desired. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Operation Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Right-click on the button to edit. Button related pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu Description Reset 3D Position Reset to location of pre-simulation. Copy Copy the selected button. Paste Paste the selected button. Mirror Paste (Position Only) Mirror paste the position of the selected button. Delete Delete the selected button. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Duplicate the selected button to its symmetric pattern. Convert to Buttonhole (ver5.0.0) Convert the selected button to a buttonhole. Activate/Deactivate Activate or deactivate the selected button. Freeze/Unfreeze Freeze or unfreeze the selected button. Set Number of Sewing Layers Set the number of sewing layers for the selected button. After setting the Number of Sewing Layers, use the Select/Move Button tool to adjust buttons' locations on each Patterns. Flip Move the selected button to the opposite side. Align Align selected buttons based on the selected options. Distribute Distribute selected buttons horizontally or vertically with same intervals

Title: [Object Browser] Button List Window
Content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

Title: [Style Property] Open/ Save Puckering Style
Content: List of Contents Open Save Objective Open or save preset or custom Puckering to easily use it in other Project or Garment files. Location Open Object Browser Puckering Tab Select Desired Puckering Style Property Editor Open Save Object Browser Puckering Tab Select Desired Puckering Style Property Editor Save Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Select Desired Puckering Style Property Editor Open The File Browser window appears. Select the desired Puckering file and click Open. The selected Puckering file opens and all properties are reflected in the Property Editor. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Select Desired Puckering Style Property Editor Save The File Save window appears. Designate the file saving path and assign Puckering name. Then, select Save. The Puckering is saved as a *.ptp file and all properties are saved.

Select and Apply a New Puckering Style Select a line where a Puckering is applied. Title: [Object Browser] Delete Puckering Style
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Puckering style. Location Object Browser Puckering Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Click on Delete icon on the right-hand side of the Puckering style to delete. The selected Puckering style is now being deleted. Note: Puckering style can only be deleted when it is not in use.

Title: [Object Browser] Copy Puckering Style
Content: Objective Make a copy of an existing Puckering style. Location Object Browser Puckering Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Select a Puckering style to copy. Once it is selected, click on the Copy button at the right top corner. A copy of the selected Puckering style is now being created.

Title: [Tool] Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (ver5.1.0)
Content: List of Contents Create Select Unlink Objective Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. Location Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Operation Create Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Right click on a Pattern Outline. The Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline window appears. Note: To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. Configure below options as needed: Start Position Distance Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. Interval Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. Replicate Interval Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. Click OK. Buttonholes are created as a group. Select Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. All buttonholes in a group are selected. Note: Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. Change selected buttonholes' properties or style or use right-click pop-up menu. Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. Note: Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. Unlink Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. The link between the buttonholes are removed.

Title: [Popup] Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
Content: Objective Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Depending on the selected item, select Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern or Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.

Title: [Style Property] Edit Puckering Style Properties
Content: List of Contents Puckering Style Setting Default Puckering Style Objective Edit or reset Puckering style properties. Location Object Browser Puckering Tab Operation Puckering Style Setting Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Click on Puckering style. Puckering style properties appear in the Property Editor. Adjust the properties as needed. Name Name the Puckering style. Material Five presets are provided: Cotton, Denim, Leather, Nylon, Polyester. Texture (ver.5.1.0) Apply the texture. Desaturation Maintain the texture of images or patterns while changing colors. Shadow Intensity Adjust the intensity of the texture's shadow. Shadow Brightness Adjust the brightness of the texture's shadow while maintaining the image's pattern and texture. Normal Map Change the Puckering's shape by importing a Normal Map. Opacity (%) Adjust the Normal Map's opacity. Specification Density (%) Adjust the density of the Normal Map. Width (mm) Adjust the width of the Normal Map. Default Puckering Style Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Puckering Tab Right click on the puckering style to make as a default, and click Reset. The selected puckering style's properties are reset to the Default Puckering's.

Title: [Property] Scale Avatars (ver 5.2)
Content: Objective Scale an OBJ imported as an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Import an OBJ as an Avatar. Select the tool/ menu indicated in Location. Select the Avatar and click the Scale button to resize the Avatar. The scale Gizmo appears. Click and drag the Gizmo's X-axis (red), Y-axis (yellow-green), Z-axis (blue) or the rectangle. The Avatar size is adjusted according to the selected direction. Click the Scale button to complete scaling. The Gizmo is changed to a standard one that is used to move or rotate the Avatar. Note: Scale with specific values in the Property Window after selecting the Avatar.

Title: Trace
Content: List of Contents Trace as a Pattern Trace as an Internal Shape Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes Trace as Point of Measure(POM) (ver 6.0) Objective Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area/guidelines (ver5.0.0) to Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Operation Trace as a Pattern Select the tool/menu indicated in Location Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as a Pattern. The selected Baselines are traced as a Pattern. Trace as an Internal Shape Select the tool/menu indicated in Location Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as an Internal Shape. When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes Select the tool/menu indicated in Location Select the Baselines to be traced. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes. The selected lines are traced as they are. Trace as POM (ver 6.0) Select the tool/menu indicated in Location Select the Baselines, Internal Lines or Outlines to be traced. Right-click on the selected lines to access the pop-up menu. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as Point of Measure The selected line is traced as POM. When more than two segments of different patterns are clicked, they are traced as a group POM. At this time, the connected points are randomly designated. Note: To easily select a closed shape, double click on the Internal Line. Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected. Occasionally, Internal Lines may not be connected precisely when dxf files are imported into CLO from other 2D CAD programs. If the selected lines are less than 0.5mm apart, they are traced as a closed shape as they are recognized as adjacent lines. However, on the other hand, if the selected lines are more than 0.5mm apart, they are traced as individual Internal Lines as they are recognized as separate lines.

Title: Connection to DMIx Cloud & Compatible with Material (ver 6.0)
Content: Objective Simply drag and drop to apply color or AxF files for CLO. Find a variety of digitalized materials &amp colors from DMIx Cloud Web of Color Digital. Operation Drag and drop AxF files into the 3D/ 2D window of CLO from the DMIx Cloud webpage. The AxF files are downloaded in DMIx Download Manager. Drag and drop AxF files to the 3D garment/ 2D Patterns or Click 'Assign to Selected Fabric' in DMIx Download Manager once you selected 3D garment/2D patterns. AxF file is applied. Note: Main Menu Preferences Clicking DMIx Download Manager also allows you to execute the window. New items are added when you drag and drop the AxF file of DMIx Download Manager to the Fabric List.

Title: Iridescence Material Expression (ver 6.0)
Content: Objective Different colors of light are reflected depending on the angle of the screen. Holographic foil, vinyl, pearls, shells of shellfish can be expressed. The application result can be checked only in the render window. Location Fabric Property Editor Material Type Iridescence (Render Only) Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Edit the properties by referring to the table below. Properties Description Color (1-5) Set the color of each area to be reflected according to the 3D screen angle. Roughness Adjust the roughness of the object surface. Hue Shift Shift the entire color spectrum to a different hue changing the 5 colors together. Weight Adjust the weight to reflect the set color on the object surface. Run the render window. The iridescent material is applied

Title: User Setting (CFG) Open/Save
Content: List of Contents Save Open Objective Save user settings such as language, measurement units, and shortcuts as a configuration file that can be applied to program updates. Location Save Main Menu File Save As User Setting Open Main Menu File Open User Setting Operation Save Configure the user settings as needed. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu File Save As User Setting The Save File window appears. Assign the file name and location, then click Save. The user settings is saved as a configuration file. Open Locate the menu as below : Main Menu File Open User Setting The Open File window appears. Select the desired configuration file and hit the Open button. The information window appears, asking you to restart the program to apply the changes. Restart the program. The user settings contained within the configuration file is applied.

Title: Trim (TRM) Open/Save
Content: List of Contents Save Open Objective Save OBJ files as Trim files. Trim files can be previewed in the CLO Library and can be glued to the Garment.. Location Save Main Menu File Save As Trim Open Main Menu File Open Trim Operation Save Load an OBJ file as Trim. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu File Save As Trim When there are multiple OBJs in the 3D window, tje Save Trim window appears allowing you to choose the desired OBJ. The Save File window appears. Locate the saving path and file name. Then, click the Save button. The OBJ file is saved Trim file. Open Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu File Open Trim The Open File window appears. Select the file to be opened and click Open. The Open Trim window appears. Use the drop-down menu next to Position option to locate the Trim. Original: trim is loaded at its original position when it was saved as a Trim file. Reset: trim is loaded at the center of the 3D window. Note: Hover the mouse over the Trim file in the Library window to preview trim. Click and drag or double lick the Trim file to open from the Library window.

Title: Animation Video Capture
Content: Objective Create video captures of animations recorded in the Animation Mode. Location Main Menu File Video Capture Animation Operation Navigate to the Animation Mode. The screen environment changes to Animation Mode. Record an animation. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Video Capture Animation The Animation window with video capture settings appears. Adjust the settings below as needed: Menu Item Description Video Size Preset Select from available presets for the video capture size. Orientation Select the video capture orientation. Width Input a specific pixel width for the video capture. Height Input a specific pixel height for the video capture. Video Codec Set the codec to use when recording video. Note: From ver 6.0, it is available to save MP4/AVI for Windows and MOV files for MAC without installing a separate codec. Click on the Record button. The animation video capture automatically starts from the beginning of the recorded Garment animation. Click on the Stop button. The animation video capture is completed and a preview window appears. Click on the Save button in the preview window. Navigate to a desired file location and input a desired file name in the window that appears. Click on the Save button after navigating to the desired file location. The animation video capture is saved. Note: While video recording, the main menu, 3D view controls, and Animation Editor functions cannot be used. Press the Pause button to pause the recording, then use the view controls to change the view, or use other functions. However, it is impossible to switch to other modes. To stop the video capture altogether, press Esc on the keyboard, click on Cancel, or X button on the top-right corner.
